dialogues.title: At the Café
dialogues.subtitle: Order a drink and make a simple request politely.
dialogues.setting: You are ordering at a small café. The barista is ready to help.

transcript.speaker: Barista
transcript.text: Good morning! What can I get for you?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Could I have a cup of coffee, please?

transcript.speaker: Barista
transcript.text: Of course. Would you like milk or sugar?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: A little milk, please. No sugar.

transcript.speaker: Barista
transcript.text: Anything else?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: That's all, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Barista
transcript.text: You're welcome. That will be forty thousand rupiah.

turns.partnerLine: Good morning! What can I get for you?
turns.prompt: You want a cup of coffee. Which response sounds polite?
options: Could I have a cup of coffee, please?
I am coffee yesterday.
Give coffee now.
turns.response: Could I have a cup of coffee, please?
turns.explanation: Could I have …, please? is a polite way to order something.

turns.partnerLine: Would you like milk or sugar?
turns.prompt: You want a little milk and no sugar. What should you say?
options: I little milk no sugar.
A little milk, please. No sugar.
I don't want coffee yesterday.
turns.response: A little milk, please. No sugar.
turns.explanation: A little milk describes your preference, and No sugar makes the request clear.

turns.prompt: You do not need anything more. How can you finish naturally?
options: That's all, thank you.
Where is your birthday?
I am finish yesterday.
turns.explanation: That's all, thank you is a natural, polite way to say your order is complete.

dialogues.title: Finding the Bus Station
dialogues.subtitle: Ask for directions and check that you understood.
dialogues.setting: You are in an unfamiliar part of town and need to find the bus station.

transcript.speaker: Local
transcript.text: Hello. Can I help you?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the bus station?

transcript.speaker: Local
transcript.text: Certainly. Go straight and turn left at the second corner.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Is it across from the post office?

transcript.speaker: Local
transcript.text: Yes, that's right. You will see it on your right.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Thank you for your help.

transcript.speaker: Local
transcript.text: No problem. It's about a five-minute walk.

turns.prompt: You need to find the bus station. Which question is the clearest?
options: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the bus station?
You bus station now?
Where you go yesterday?
turns.response: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the bus station?
turns.explanation: Excuse me softens the request, and could you tell me how to get to… clearly asks for directions.

turns.partnerLine: Go straight and turn left at the second corner.
turns.prompt: You want to check a landmark. What is a natural follow-up?
options: Is it across from the post office?
Does the post office eat lunch?
I arrive the corner yesterday.
turns.response: Is it across from the post office?
turns.explanation: Asking about a nearby landmark is a useful way to confirm that you understood the directions.

turns.partnerLine: Yes, that's right. You will see it on your right.
turns.prompt: The directions are clear. How should you close the conversation?
options: Thank you for your help.
I am the bus station.
You are welcome me.
turns.explanation: Thank you for your help is a polite closing after someone gives you directions.

dialogues.title: Planning a Study Session
dialogues.subtitle: Suggest a plan, explain a delay, and respond cooperatively.
dialogues.setting: Your group has to finish a presentation by Friday. You are discussing how to share the work.

transcript.speaker: Nadia
transcript.text: We need to finish our group presentation by Friday. How should we divide the work?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: I suggest that we each prepare one section and review the slides together.

transcript.speaker: Nadia
transcript.text: That sounds reasonable. Are you available to meet tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: I can meet after class, but I may be ten minutes late because of a bus delay.

transcript.speaker: Nadia
transcript.text: No problem. Could you still review the introduction before then?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Of course. I'll read it tonight and share my comments.

turns.partnerLine: How should we divide the work?
turns.prompt: You want to propose a fair plan. Which response is the most constructive?
options: I suggest that we each prepare one section and review the slides together.
You do everything because I am busy.
The presentation is Friday yesterday.
turns.response: I suggest that we each prepare one section and review the slides together.
turns.explanation: I suggest that… introduces an idea politely, while each prepare one section makes the division of work clear.

turns.partnerLine: Are you available to meet tomorrow?
turns.prompt: You can meet after class, but your bus may be delayed. What is the clearest response?
options: I can meet after class, but I may be ten minutes late because of a bus delay.
I available yesterday after class.
No, I meeting bus.
turns.response: I can meet after class, but I may be ten minutes late because of a bus delay.
turns.explanation: This response confirms when you are available and explains the possible delay without cancelling the meeting.

turns.partnerLine: Could you still review the introduction before then?
turns.prompt: You agree to help. Which response gives a clear next step?
options: Of course. I'll read it tonight and share my comments.
Maybe the introduction is a chair.
You should review yesterday.
turns.response: Of course. I'll read it tonight and share my comments.
turns.explanation: Of course accepts the request, and the second sentence explains exactly what you will do and when.

dialogues.title: Revising a Project Proposal
dialogues.subtitle: Challenge an assumption, weigh consequences, and suggest a workable alternative.
dialogues.setting: Your student team has proposed a campus study-space project. A new cost estimate means the group must revise its plan before presenting it to the student council.

focusWords.meaning: cukup besar atau penting dalam jumlah, nilai, atau pengaruh
melemahkan secara bertahap; mengurangi kekuatan atau kepercayaan

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: The revised estimate shows a substantial increase in the equipment cost. I am worried that the current proposal is no longer realistic.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: I agree that the increase changes our assumptions. However, removing the quiet study area entirely could undermine the main purpose of the project.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: That is a fair point. What alternative would you suggest?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: We could open the quiet area in phases and use the first month's feedback to decide what equipment is essential.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: That would reduce the initial cost, although we should be clear about the consequences of delaying the second phase.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Absolutely. We can include a review date and explain that the second phase depends on usage and the remaining budget.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Good. Let's revise the proposal and make those conditions explicit before Friday.

turns.partnerLine: The revised estimate shows a substantial increase in the equipment cost. I am worried that the current proposal is no longer realistic.
turns.prompt: You want to acknowledge the concern without abandoning the project's main purpose. Which response is strongest?
options: I agree the increase changes our assumptions, but removing the quiet area could undermine the project's main purpose.
The estimate is wrong, so we should ignore it.
I do not care about the cost because the idea is important.
turns.response: I agree the increase changes our assumptions, but removing the quiet area could undermine the project's main purpose.
turns.explanation: The response recognises the new evidence while explaining why the original objective still matters. Could undermine describes how a decision may weaken the project's purpose.

turns.partnerLine: That is a fair point. What alternative would you suggest?
turns.prompt: You want to reduce the initial cost while keeping the project possible. What is the most practical suggestion?
options: We should buy everything immediately and hope the budget works.
We could open the quiet area in phases and review feedback before buying the remaining equipment.
We should cancel the project without discussing any other option.
turns.response: We could open the quiet area in phases and review feedback before buying the remaining equipment.
turns.explanation: A phased approach is a realistic alternative: it limits the initial commitment and uses evidence before the next decision.

turns.partnerLine: That would reduce the initial cost, although we should be clear about the consequences of delaying the second phase.
turns.prompt: How should you respond to make the proposal more accountable?
options: There will be no consequences, so there is nothing to explain.
Let's leave that detail out of the presentation.
We can set a review date and explain that the second phase depends on usage and the remaining budget.
turns.response: We can set a review date and explain that the second phase depends on usage and the remaining budget.
turns.explanation: A review date and clear conditions make the consequences visible and give the team a measurable basis for continuing.
